Seniors shouldn’t jump through bureaucratic hoops to access essential care. H.R. 1517 fixes Medicare’s outdated restrictions by finally allowing physical therapists to use locum tenens arrangements—a common-sense solution to prevent treatment gaps. This bill exposes how Medicare’s rigid rules prioritize paperwork over patients, forcing therapists to choose between compliance and continuity of care.

The $2,230 annual threshold for “medical necessity” reviews creates needless delays—meanwhile, agencies burn billions on redundant administrative bloat. Physical therapy isn’t optional—it’s critical for maintaining independence.

Cutting red tape here is a win, but real reform requires auditing Medicare’s entire reimbursement system to stop rationing care through complexity.

The Resident Physician Shortage Reduction Act (H.R. 3890) exposes Washington's decades-long failure to address the physician pipeline crisis. While adding 14,000 Medicare-funded residency slots over seven years is necessary, the real issue is systemic mismanagement: 86% of rural counties already face primary care shortages while bureaucrats protected a frozen GME system since 1997.

This bill’s rural carveouts and HPSA prioritization are Band-Aids on a hemorrhage caused by central planning. True reform requires dismantling the AMA/AAMC monopoly on accreditation, forcing hospitals to redirect administrative bloat savings into training, and ending the fiction that 75-position caps per hospital constitute "ambitious" growth.

Until Medicare's $150B annual waste gets reined in, even 14,000 new slots risk becoming another unfunded mandate buried under bureaucracy.

The real story is in the numbers and the entrenched interests—see the full breakdown: https://t.co/uJOpQXis6t
